title: Neural Networks
description: From a neuron to a trained net: nonlinearities, backpropagation, representations, and why sequence models forget. Attention is the next course.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS229
sourceReferences.notes: Neural nets after linear models and generalization. Training is a separate lecture from the architecture.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS224N
sourceReferences.notes: Embeddings and RNNs before attention, even in years that compress the calendar. Assumes ML foundations.

modules.title: Networks
learningObjectives: Compose weighted sums and nonlinearities into a multilayer map
Explain why a stack without a nonlinearity is still one line

modules.title: Training nets
modules.blurb: Backprop, initialization, and the ways training dies.
learningObjectives: Backpropagate a scalar loss to every weight
Name a reason gradients vanish, explode, or fail to start

modules.title: Representations
modules.blurb: Embeddings, convolutions, and sequences before attention.
learningObjectives: Treat an embedding or convolution as an inductive bias, not magic features
Reuse a representation trained on a different job

concepts.name: The artificial neuron
concepts.summary: A weighted sum, a bias, and a nonlinearity.
objectives: Write an artificial neuron as a weighted sum, a bias, and a nonlinearity
Predict the output when the nonlinearity is removed

concepts.name: Nonlinearities
concepts.summary: Without one, a stack of layers is still a line.
objectives: Explain why a stack of linear layers without a nonlinearity is still one line
Compare ReLU, sigmoid, and tanh on saturation and gradient flow

concepts.name: Multilayer perceptrons
concepts.summary: Layers of neurons, each a function of the last.
objectives: Compose layers of neurons so each layer is a function of the last
Trace a small forward pass from input vector to output score

concepts.name: Softmax
concepts.summary: Turning scores into a distribution over classes.
objectives: Turn a vector of scores into a distribution over classes
Predict what happens to the probabilities if one score dominates

concepts.name: Cross-entropy
concepts.summary: The usual loss when the output is a distribution.
objectives: Use cross-entropy when the output is a distribution over classes
State why cross-entropy plus softmax is the usual classification pair

concepts.name: Why depth
concepts.summary: Composition of simple functions instead of one wide shallow map.
objectives: Explain depth as composing simple functions instead of one wide shallow map
Name a function that a shallow net needs far more width to match

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.summary: Reverse-mode autodiff, not a separate algorithm from calculus.
objectives: Describe backpropagation as reverse-mode autodiff on a scalar loss
Trace a local Jacobian backward so every weight receives a partial

concepts.name: Reverse-mode autodiff
concepts.summary: One backward pass gives every partial you need.
objectives: Contrast reverse-mode (one backward, every partial) with forward-mode
Predict why one loss and millions of parameters choose reverse mode

concepts.name: Initialization
concepts.summary: Where the weights start decides whether gradients survive.
objectives: Choose an initialization so activations and gradients start at a usable scale
Diagnose a start that saturates sigmoids or explodes products

concepts.name: Vanishing and exploding gradients
concepts.summary: A product of many derivatives that goes to zero or infinity.
objectives: Describe vanishing or exploding gradients as a product of many derivatives
Predict which activation and depth combinations make the product die

concepts.name: Momentum and adaptive methods
concepts.summary: Remembering recent slopes, scaling per-parameter.
objectives: Add momentum or a per-parameter scale so recent slopes are remembered
Compare plain SGD with a momentum or adaptive update on a ravine

concepts.name: Normalization layers
concepts.summary: Re-centering activations so the next layer sees a stable input.
objectives: Re-center and re-scale activations so the next layer sees a stable input
Predict what batch norm does to the training versus inference pass

concepts.name: Dropout
concepts.summary: Training as an ensemble of thinned nets.
objectives: Train as an ensemble of thinned nets by dropping units at random
Predict why dropout is off at inference and how the remaining weights are scaled

concepts.name: Overparameterization
concepts.summary: More parameters than data points — and it can still generalize.
objectives: State that more parameters than data points can still generalize
Contrast interpolation of the sample with memorization that fails off the sample

concepts.name: Inductive bias
concepts.summary: What the architecture refuses to represent.
objectives: Define inductive bias as what the architecture refuses to represent
Name a structure a fully connected net wastes capacity relearning

concepts.name: Convolutions
concepts.summary: Weight sharing across space because the world repeats.
objectives: Share weights across space because the same pattern can appear anywhere
Predict what a convolution sees that a dense layer must relearn at every position

concepts.name: Embeddings
concepts.summary: A learned lookup from a discrete symbol to a vector.
objectives: Describe an embedding as a learned lookup from a discrete symbol to a vector
Predict why nearby symbols should not start as nearby integers

concepts.name: Learned representations
concepts.summary: Features the model invented instead of features you wrote.
objectives: Treat a later layer as features the model invented, not features you wrote
Name what a downstream job can reuse from that representation

concepts.name: Distributional embeddings
concepts.summary: You shall know a word by the company it keeps.
objectives: Learn a word vector from the company it keeps
Predict a geometric analogy the distributional objective can and cannot justify

concepts.name: Recurrent sequence models
concepts.summary: A hidden state that walks the sequence.
objectives: Walk a sequence with a hidden state that is a function of the previous state
Trace what the state must remember to map a long input onto an output

concepts.name: Why RNNs forget
concepts.summary: The same vanishing product, now across time.
objectives: Explain RNN forgetting as the same vanishing product, now across time
Predict why a distant token's gradient dies in a vanilla recurrence

concepts.name: Transfer learning, first look
concepts.summary: Reuse a representation trained on a different job.
objectives: Reuse a representation trained on a different job
Predict when the old features help and when they are the wrong inductive bias
